name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
principle: The product embeds a fixed cryptographic key in code, binary, firmware, or bundled configuration. Anyone who extracts it can decrypt data, forge signatures/tokens, bypass access control, and the key is hard to rotate.
detection_signals: JWT signing call with literal key: Jwts.parser().setSigningKey("...") or signWith(..., "...")
PEM private key literal or resource: "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----" or "-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----"
C/C++ static const unsigned char key[] = { ... } used by AES_set_encrypt_key|HMAC|EVP_EncryptInit_ex
strcmp|equals comparing input to fixed high-entropy hex/base64 string used as a key or privileged verifier
negative_signals: key material fetched from KMS/HSM API: AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Google Cloud KMS, PKCS#11
Java KeyStore.getKey(alias, password) with keystore path/password not hard-coded
key generated at install/runtime with KeyGenerator|KeyPairGenerator|SecureRandom and persisted securely
only public certificate/public key is embedded: "BEGIN CERTIFICATE" or "BEGIN PUBLIC KEY" with no private/secret key
literal is a test vector under test/ or src/test/ and not used in production code path
false_defense_traps: Base64, hex, XOR, or string splitting hides the key but does not protect it from extraction
Compiling into a binary or firmware image does not prevent reverse engineering of embedded keys
Putting the same key in a bundled config file is still hard-coded if shipped with the product
Using one factory/default key for all devices makes one extraction compromise every instance
Environment variable fallback to a hard-coded default key is still vulnerable when the variable is unset
verification_focus: Is a secret/private cryptographic key fixed in code, binary, firmware, or shipped config instead of being externally managed, unique, and rotatable?

consequence_chains.trigger: code relies on hiding a fixed key in the product
consequence_chains.consequence: attacker extracts the key and bypasses cryptographic protection

consequence_chains.trigger: hard-coded key functions as an authentication credential
consequence_chains.consequence: attacker assumes identity or gains privileged access

patch_principle: Remove cryptographic keys from source code, binaries, firmware, and shipped configuration.
Store keys in KMS, HSM, OS credential store, or a protected keystore separate from code.
Generate unique keys per deployment/device/account; never reuse one vendor default key.
Support key rotation and revocation without rebuilding or patching the product.
Fail closed when an external key is missing; do not use a hard-coded fallback key.
